study type: Interrupted time series analysis, retrospective study
exposure: Hospital policy changes related to the COVID-19 pandemic
outcome: Early discharge (<48 hours after cesarean and <24 hours after vaginal births)
cohort: Consecutive singleton births at 15 hospitals in the Pacific Northwest, United States, from 2017 to 2020
finding: The study found increases in early discharge and newborn readmission rates among nulliparous women after the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic, while multiparous women experienced decreases in preterm birth, low 5-minute Apgar score, and term NICU admission rates.
mod_finding: The study found no statistically significant changes in mode of delivery after the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic.
